bib.title: Social Simulacra: Creating Populated Prototypes for Social Computing Systems

question: Can an LLM populate a draft social-computing design (goal, rules, personas) with realistic simulated behaviour so a designer can anticipate and fix problems before launch?
hypothesis: LLMs' training data already contains diverse pro- and anti-social online behaviour, so prompt chains can generate plausible populated communities that help designers iterate.
contributions: Social simulacra, a prototyping technique that generates populated social behaviour from a design description
Prompt-chain techniques for GPT-3 generating thousands of distinct members and their interactions
SimReddit tool with Generate, WhatIf and Multiverse
A technical evaluation on 50 unseen subreddits and a study with 16 designers

method.summary: SimReddit expands ~10 designer seed personas into 1,000 with a few-shot GPT-3 prompt, then generates top-level posts and replies by prompting base davinci with persona, rules and HTML span templates, stopping at the closing tag. WhatIf swaps the replier persona or injects a moderator comment; Multiverse resamples at temperature 0.8.
method.task: generating simulated social media community interactions for design prototyping

datasets.name: 50 post-GPT-3 subreddits
datasets.source: top five largest subreddits per creation date from 2020-06-11 via frontpagemetrics.com, English only
datasets.preprocessing: real threads: >=200 posts behind latest, text-only, >=3 responses, truncated to first 5

models.name: GPT-3 davinci (base, released 2020-06-11)
models.context: inferred: input limited to roughly 8,000 characters

inference.decoding: API sampling; generation stopped at closing tag
inference.samples: Multiverse: repeated regeneration (number not stated); designer study showed 3 WhatIf generations per prompt
inference.prompting: Zero-shot template prompts with persona description, rules as 'not X' phrases, HTML span tags (class headline_reddit / comment max_200_words, title with rules); few-shot for persona expansion; thread history in prompt, truncated from first post

parameters.reply probability p: drawn from N(.65, stdev); stdev not stated
parameters.new persona rate: 50% new persona, else one already in conversation (not the latest speaker)

metrics.name: error rate
metrics.definition: fraction of real-vs-synthetic pairs where participant picked the synthetic one as real; 50% is chance

baselines: Crowdworker conversations (10 Prolific workers per subreddit in a Google Doc)
eval.protocol: Between-subjects, 50 participants per condition (200 total, power analysis alpha 0.05 power 80%), 100 comparisons, one-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD; designer study with 16 designers, think-aloud and inductive coding

prompts.text: Layla Li is a college student studying to be a social worker. She shares comments that are not encouraging suicide, not anti-therapy, not trolling, not incivility, not self-marketing. Layla posted the following headline to an online forum for sharing your psychotherapy stories and questions: <span class="headline_reddit" title="comment that is about psychotherapy, and NOT encouraging suicide, NOT anti-therapy">
[Troll] shares trolling comments. ... [Troll]: <span class="comment max_200_words" title="comment that is trolling">"

results.claim: Participants misidentified the SimReddit conversation as real in 41% of pairs, close to the 50% chance level.
results.setup: 50 unseen subreddits, 50 participants in the SimReddit condition, GPT-3 davinci, real vs generated pairs
results.quote: their error rate was 41% (std=10%) on average

results.claim: Crowdworker baseline had a lower error rate than SimReddit.
results.setup: same task, crowdworker-written conversations vs real
results.quote: where the error rate was only 32% (std=13%)

results.claim: Removing the community description dropped the error rate to 21%.
results.setup: SimReddit without community goal and rules in prompt

results.claim: Removing personas lowered the error rate (text says 33%, Table 1 says 34%).
results.setup: SimReddit with users numbered, no persona descriptions

results.claim: Omnibus ANOVA across the four conditions is significant.
results.setup: one-way ANOVA on error rate, 200 participants

results.claim: All 16 designers found unexpected insights in initial generations and all but one revised their design.
results.table: Section 6.4.3 (15 of 16 revised; n=15 for failure-case revisions)

results.claim: 14 of 16 designers said the generations were realistic, yet 15 noticed unlikely aspects.
13 of 16 designers found it daunting to envision design success and failure before the study.

limits: Does not predict outcomes; authors say single-point prediction is impossible (7.2.1).
False negatives: even with Multiverse, outputs are not exhaustive; implied truth effect risk (7.1.1).
Text-only, English-only, Reddit-only; GPT-3 prompt limit about 8,000 characters forces truncation of earlier conversation (7.2.3).
Technical eval checks only real-vs-fake plausibility on first-5-response threads, not fidelity of group dynamics; the designer study has no outcome measure of community quality after launch.
Models may reproduce biases in who participates; risks of astroturfing and harassment tooling (7.3).
Base davinci lacks knowledge after mid-2020 (e.g. COVID-19); covidlonghaulers example failed.
Prompt chains are single-turn persona prompting; no agent memory, planning or tools; no multi-agent interaction loop beyond sampled turn-taking.

terms.definition: a prototyping technique that generates a breadth of realistic social interactions that may emerge when a social computing system is populated
